summary: An applicability statement for OSPF, placing a requirement on vendors claiming conformance so that users can deploy OSPF in multivendor networks. It is historic.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo says when a router vendor must implement OSPF. Its goal is to give users a common routing option across products from different vendors.

questions: what features of ospf are mandatory
what did rfc 1370 require router vendors to implement
subtitle: Requirements for router vendors claiming conformance to the OSPF applicability statement.

tldr.problem: Users needed assurance that routers from different vendors could use a common, open interior gateway protocol.
tldr.mechanism: This applicability statement requires an IP router that implements a routing protocol other than static routes to implement OSPF and its MIB. Type-of-Service routing is recommended but not required.
tldr.outcome: RFC 1370 is Historic. It stated OSPF implementation requirements for vendors claiming conformance and allowed additional routing protocols.

today: RFC 1370 is marked Historic in the unit metadata. It set OSPF implementation requirements for a particular stage of the router standards process.

sections.title: The Need for a Common IGP
sections.content:
The Internet Architecture Board says users and vendors wanted IP routers from different vendors to interoperate through a common Interior Gateway Protocol (IGP). The IETF developed Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) to meet that need as a non-proprietary protocol.

This applicability statement sets requirements for vendors claiming conformance. It does not require users to choose OSPF; they remain free to use the routing protocol that best meets their needs.
sections.plainLanguage: Different router makers needed a shared way to exchange routes. This memo sets a minimum OSPF requirement for routers that support routing.

sections.title: Router Implementation Requirements
sections.content:
An IP router that implements any routing protocol other than static routes is required to implement OSPF and the OSPF Management Information Base. Within OSPF, all features except Type-of-Service routing are required; Type-of-Service routing is recommended.

The requirement does not prevent a router from implementing other protocols too. The memo says broader requirements for IP routers were being prepared and would take precedence if they later conflicted with this statement.
sections.plainLanguage: A router that supports routing must include OSPF and its management information. It may support other routing protocols as well.

sections.title: Routers, Not Hosts
sections.content:
OSPF is intended for routers exchanging dynamic routing information, not for hosts. The memo discourages hosts from listening in on routing protocols and points to host requirements and ICMP Router Discovery as ways for a host to learn about local routers.

The security considerations section says security issues are not discussed in this memo.
sections.plainLanguage: OSPF is for routers to share route information. A host should use host-specific methods to discover its local router.
